newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian new PM vows to restore order, economy.
newsitem.headline: Albanian new PM vows to restore order, economy.

text.p: Albania's new Socialist Prime Minister Fatos Nano said on Monday his leftist coalition government would move quickly to restore order and warned the economic outlook looked bleak.

Nano, whose Socialist Party and its allies won 119 seats in the 155-seat parliament in a general election last month, also pledged to compensate Albanians who lost their savings in pyramid investment schemes.

The collapse of the schemes earlier this year led to protests, violence and the breakdown of law and order, sparking months of chaos and led to the ousting of the right-leaning Democratic Party from government and the resignation of president Sali Berisha last week.
"Re-establishing law and order will be the first priority of the new government," Nano said in his first speech to parliament.
He said his government would re-establish peace and security in towns, make safe highways from armed bands of looters and aim to collect weapons looted from army and police depots.

Nano, who took office as Prime Minister on Friday, painted a bleak economic picture for Albania, saying his government hoped to halt the decline of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), which plummeted drastically during the unrest. GDP had risen 9.1 percent in 1996.
"The objective of the government would be to stop the further decline of GDP," Nano said. He added GDP in 1997 was planned to be around 415 billion leks ($2.4 billion) at current prices.
The budget deficit was planned to reach 44 billion leks, 11.6 percent of GDP, and inflation was expected to rise to 45-50 percent by the end of the year.

Nano, a 44-year-old economist, said his government would secure revenue by ensuring tax administration and especially customs offices began functioning normally and that authorities would crack down on tax evasion.
Customs duties could be cut if tax evasion were reduced to a minimum, he added.
Nano pledged to push towards the setting up a new constitution which would guarantee human rights, the independence of the judiciary and respect for democratic legislation.
Nano needs to win approval of his government plan in a vote in parliament on Tuesday but there was little doubt he would the secure necessary backing.
